en-GB.title: The Interaction of Leverage and Risk
en-GB.summary: The Interaction of Leverage and Risk
en-GB.body: Leverage uses borrowed money to control an asset larger than the investor's cash contribution. It magnifies both gains and losses measured against invested capital. Debt also creates fixed payment obligations that continue during vacancies, repairs and downturns. More leverage therefore reduces room for error unless supported by adequate cash flow and reserves. Level 2 thinking evaluates both upside and survivability rather than viewing leverage only as a way to increase returns.
